subject: Re: POC Trial - Model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@globex.com>
Cc: Carlos Medina <c.medina@globex.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC follow-up: model selection & success criteria

Thanks for taking the time today, Sofia 
 great conversation. Quick recap and proposed plan for the POC/trial so we have aligned success criteria and next steps.

Call recap / goals:
- Evaluate model quality for customer-facing summarization and multilingual support (EN/ES/PT).
- Validate latency and cost targets for a pilot production footprint.
- Confirm data flows and security evidence for procurement.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or adjust):
1) Quality: >85% accept rate on a 100-sample prompt set (customer labeled) for EN and >80% for ES/PT (multilingual).
2) Latency: median token generation latency <200ms on our dedicated trial capacity for typical 512-token requests.
3) Throughput/cost: sustain 5 rps at p95 latency SLO and per-token cost under $0.02 (target for pilot).
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate across 2-week evaluation window.

Model recommendation for the trial:
- Primary model: Llama2-Chat 13B (quantized, fp16/8-bit fallback) 
 chosen for balance between quality and cost and good community evaluations for summarization.
- Fallback model: MPT-7B-Instruct (lighter-weight) in case of capacity constraints or for cheaper throughput during batched evaluation.
- Multilingual handling: use the 13B as primary; we'll route Spanish/Portuguese prompts to the same model and include language-specific prompt templates. If quality falls short, we will include an ES-finetuned variant as an optional follow-up.

Next steps / timeline (proposal):
- By 2026-06-18: finalize success criteria and sign-off on model selection (your team).
- By 2026-06-22: provide POC access credentials and dedicated trial pool (Redwood to provision).
- 2026-06-24 to 2026-07-08: 2-week evaluation window (Globex runs labeled prompts + Redwood runs throughput/latency tests).
- By 2026-07-10: joint review and decision on pilot rollout or model adjustments.

Ownership:
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao (technical provisioning, test harness)
- Redwood CS: Laura Bennett (evaluation coordination, sample collection)
- Globex POC lead: Sofia Ramos (acceptance, sample labeling)

I've attached an initial evaluation matrix (MVP_evaluation_matrix.xlsx) with suggested prompt sets and metrics. Please confirm the success criteria and ownership so we can lock the schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: MVP_evaluation_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

Thanks Marissa 
 this looks good and aligns with our internal priorities. A few quick notes/questions:

- Success criteria: the quality thresholds look reasonable. We'll run the 100-sample set and add an extra 50 Spanish/Portuguese items for edge cases.
- Latency / cost: we need Redwood to run a baseline perf test on the 13B quantized model so we can compare against our internal budget.
- Security: please include SOC2 and data handling docs. I've cc'd our security mailbox (it-security@globex.com) 
 they will request evidence and may ask for an architecture diagram.

Timeline: the proposed schedule works. We can confirm sign-off by Thursday (2026-06-18).

One ask: can you also include the fallback model behavior in the evaluation matrix (when to trigger fallback and how we measure regressions)?

Sofia Ramos

sofia.ramos@globex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC follow-up: model selection & success criteria

Appreciate the quick reply, Sofia. Responses inline and updated plan below.

- Baseline perf test: Aditya will run an initial perf sweep on the quantized Llama2-Chat 13B and produce a short report (median/p95 latency, throughput at target batch sizes).
- Security docs: attaching POC_access_instructions.pdf which includes architecture diagram, data handling notes, and a link to our SOC2 evidence bundle (drive link below).
- Fallback behavior: we'll add explicit fallback rules to the matrix. High-level: if p95 latency for a route exceeds 350ms or error rate >1.5% for 10 minutes, route new sessions to MPT-7B-Instruct for that tenant. We'll log metrics and run a quality-sampled check for 50 prompts when fallback is triggered.

Updated timeline and owners:
- 2026-06-18: Globex sign-off on success criteria (Sofia).
- 2026-06-22: Redwood provisions trial environment + initial model loads (Aditya).
- 2026-06-24 to 2026-07-08: Evaluation window: combined quality and perf tests (Laura coordinates).
- 2026-07-09 to 2026-07-10: Joint review meeting (Marissa + Sofia + Laura + Aditya).

I've attached the updated evaluation matrix with fallback rules and perf checklist. Let us know if you want the drive folder shared with additional Globex users.

Thanks,
Marissa
